content_of_post_to_comment: You can very easily convert between "materialist", "panpsychist" and "objective idealist" conceptions of the world by describing the exact same things, working in the exact same way and just swapping out the words for words of a different emotional valence or general vibe. "Existence" becomes "consciousness" or "experience" (which has no bearing on human experience which is nevertheless a very complex and derived thing in either case) "quantum field" becomes "world mind", "particles" become "elementary thoughts" or something like that. And you can make a lot of people very angry or very excited, while in reality you've said uncontroversial statements worded in an odd way,- or perhaps it was worded in an odd way and you fixed it, if you like, but either way it makes no practical difference to anything worth caring about. As a concrete example, if you think the existence of an afterlife is impossible in an entirely "material" universe, you sadly don't have the skills to write good sci-fi. If only getting rid of ghosts were that easy. You know marketing people did these experiments where they rephrased slogans like "protect the environment" as "defend our habitat" or something, and suddenly right-wingers became more open to the messaging? Yeah it's like that.
comment: A fascinating tension is that language may reshape intuitions without changing ontology, but intuitions often drive what questions people consider worth asking. The framing itself can alter the philosophy.
